title: Fisherman Trapped Under Boulder in Astoria, Oregon, Saved After Using Siri to Call 911
text:
A fisherman trapped under a boulder in Astoria, Oregon, used Siri to call 911 and was rescued. He is now recovering from severe facial injuries.
A 28-year-old fisherman, Joe Little, was rescued after being trapped under a massive boulder in Astoria, Oregon, on Saturday morning. Little, who was fishing alone at the Hammond Marina jetty, used Siri on his iPhone to call 911 around 7 a.m. after the boulder pinned him down. He is now recovering in a Portland hospital with severe facial injuries.
How Siri Saved a Trapped Fisherman
Little was fishing when a huge rock tumbled and trapped him under the high tide line. His grandmother, Kelly Simonson, said he felt the boulder start to move and tried to stop it with his feet, but it was too large and he slipped. Trapped and unable to move, Little knew he had to act quickly to avoid drowning as the tide rose.
Fortunately, his Bluetooth earbuds were still connected to his phone, allowing him to activate Siri and call 911. His mother, Mindy, said it was a miracle that her son is alive. Little is now facing an 8-hour facial reconstruction surgery for his injuries.
Rescue Operation and Challenges
Sgt. Dylan McCoy of the Astoria Police Department said officers located Little by honking their car horns while a dispatcher asked him if the sound was getting closer. They then flew a drone and found him crushed beneath the boulder, with only his upper body and feet visible.
First responders removed smaller rocks to free him from under the extremely large boulder. However, the terrain was too dangerous to move him on foot, so they called the U.S. Coast Guard for assistance. A USCG helicopter arrived and airlifted Little in a gurney.
Recovery and Family's Relief
Little is recovering at a hospital in Portland, where he is being treated for severe facial injuries, including a broken jaw. His mother, Mindy, said his face was smashed and he is almost unrecognizable, but she is grateful he survived. The family expressed relief and credited the quick thinking and technology for saving his life.
The incident highlights the potential of technology in emergencies and the importance of quick response. Little's use of Siri to call for help while trapped underscores how accessible tools can be lifesaving in critical situations.
